title: Psycho-physiological restoration with audio-visual interactions through virtual reality simulations of soundscape and landscape experiences in urban, waterfront, and green environments

findings.mechanism: Various noises in the urban environment contribute to lower tranquility.
findings.quote: Given various noises in the urban environment, the mean factor score for tranquil soundscape was -0.94

findings.mechanism: Various noises in the urban environment contribute to higher perceived detriment.
findings.quote: the mean factor score for detrimental soundscape was very high, being 0.82.

findings.mechanism: Waterfronts are perceived as calm.
findings.quote: the mean factor score of a waterfront for tranquil soundscape, 0.19, was slightly higher than that of a green space.

findings.mechanism: Green spaces are perceived as pleasant.
findings.quote: Green space had a high factor score for supportive soundscape, 0.22

findings.mechanism: High-rise buildings and vehicles contribute to lower attractive landscape perception.
findings.quote: the factor score for attractive landscape was extremely low (-0.59) in urban environments

findings.mechanism: High-rise buildings and vehicles contribute to higher discomforting landscape perception.
findings.quote: that for discomforting landscape was high (0.57). The differences were statistically significant.

findings.mechanism: High-rise buildings and vehicles contribute to lower spatial/natural landscape perception.
findings.quote: The factor score for spatial/natural land- scape was extremely low (-0.81) in urban environments

findings.mechanism: Panoramic views (ocean, wetland) contribute to higher spatial/natural landscape perception.
findings.quote: whereas the corresponding score for waterfront with panoramic views (such as ocean and wetland) was extremely high (0.87).

findings.consequent: overall soundscape quality (overall impression, appropriateness, sound satisfaction)
findings.mechanism: Urban noise and artificial elements negatively impact overall soundscape perception.
findings.quote: all mean values of overall impression, appropriateness, and sound satisfaction were statistically significantly lower in the urban environment

findings.consequent: overall landscape quality (scenic beauty, visual satisfaction)
findings.mechanism: Natural elements enhance scenic beauty and visual satisfaction.
findings.quote: most mean values of scenic beauty and visual satisfaction in the natural environment were 4.1 or higher

findings.mechanism: Downtown areas generally have better infrastructure.
findings.quote: The mean value of the status of infrastructure was 4.1 in the urban environment, being statistically significantly higher than in the natural environment

findings.mechanism: Natural environments facilitate involuntary attention (fascination) and a sense of escaping from daily life.
findings.quote: The mean PRSS score was 4.41 in the natural environment and 2.92 in the urban environment, indicating a greater psychological restoration effect in the former.

findings.mechanism: Urban environments lead to feelings of confinement, hindering the sense of 'breaking away'.
findings.quote: Compared to the reference, 'breaking away' was very low in the urban environments at 1.93

findings.mechanism: Natural environments provide a strong sense of escaping from daily life and responsibilities.
findings.quote: extremely high in the natural envi- ronments, with 4.91 in the waterfront, and 5.02 in the green space.

findings.mechanism: Natural environments provide a strong sense of escaping from daily life and responsibilities.
findings.quote: extremely high in the natural envi- ronments, with 4.91 in the waterfront, and 5.02 in the green space.

findings.mechanism: Urban environments are perceived as less pleasant.
findings.quote: the corresponding score was statistically significantly lower in the urban environment (4.6)

findings.mechanism: Natural environments are perceived as more pleasant.
findings.quote: higher in the natural environment (6.7 in the waterfront and 6.5 in the green space).

findings.mechanism: Urban environments induce higher states of activation and excitement.
findings.quote: the mean score for arousal, a state of activation and excitement, was the highest in the urban environment (4.7)

findings.mechanism: Natural environments allow participants to maintain psychological stability and reduce negative emotions.
findings.quote: In the natural environment, however, the negative effect was statistically significantly lower than in the reference.

findings.mechanism: Waterfront exposure leads to increased overall activation level of the autonomic nervous system, indicating restoration.
findings.quote: exposure to waterfront showed a large rate of increase, over 10.5%, compared to the reference, and the increase was statistically significant.

findings.consequent: standard deviation of normal to normal (SDNN) of HRV
findings.mechanism: Waterfront exposure increases stress resistance and psychological stability.
findings.quote: SDNN increased by 13.9% and TSI decreased by 9.4%.

findings.mechanism: Waterfront exposure reduces stress and fatigue.
findings.quote: SDNN increased by 13.9% and TSI decreased by 9.4%.

findings.consequent: standard deviation of normal to normal (SDNN) of HRV
findings.mechanism: Green space exposure increases stress resistance and psychological stability.
findings.quote: Similar findings were observed in the green space, where SDNN increased (14.6%) and TSI decreased (9.5%) compared to the reference.

findings.mechanism: Green space exposure reduces stress and fatigue.
findings.quote: Similar findings were observed in the green space, where SDNN increased (14.6%) and TSI decreased (9.5%) compared to the reference.

findings.consequent: standard deviation of normal to normal (SDNN) of HRV
findings.mechanism: Participants familiar with urban stimuli may adjust to environmental changes, leading to increased stress resistance.
findings.quote: Interestingly, SDNN significantly increased in urban en- vironments compared to the reference.

findings.antecedent: exposure to any environment (urban, waterfront, green)
findings.mechanism: Stimuli in quiet surroundings generally accelerate HR, and more pleasant/eventful environments can also increase HR.
findings.quote: HR increased statistically significantly in all environ- ments compared to the reference.

findings.consequent: Positive Affect and Negative Affect Scale (PANAS) positive domains
findings.mechanism: Higher perceived restorativeness is associated with more positive emotions.
findings.quote: PRSS indicators have a statistically significant positive correlation with the positive domains of PANAS

findings.mechanism: Higher perceived restorativeness is associated with greater pleasure.
findings.quote: PRSS indicators have a statistically significant positive correlation with... the valance domain of SAM.

findings.consequent: Positive Affect and Negative Affect Scale (PANAS) negative domains
findings.mechanism: Higher perceived restorativeness is associated with fewer negative emotions.
findings.quote: the negative domain of PANAS and the arousal domain of SAM show a statistically significant negative correlation.

findings.mechanism: Higher perceived restorativeness is associated with lower arousal.
findings.quote: the negative domain of PANAS and the arousal domain of SAM show a statistically significant negative correlation.

findings.mechanism: A sense of liberation from the environment can induce psychological recovery and sympathetic nervous system vitalization.
findings.quote: the 'being away to' and 'being away from' indicators of the PRSS indicators show a weak but statistically significant positive relationship with TP

findings.consequent: standard deviation of normal to normal (SDNN) of HRV
findings.mechanism: A sense of liberation from the environment can induce psychological recovery and sympathetic nervous system vitalization.
findings.quote: the 'being away to' and 'being away from' indicators of the PRSS indicators show a weak but statistically significant positive relationship with... SDNN

findings.antecedent: PRSS 'being away to' and 'being away from' indicators
findings.mechanism: A sense of liberation from the environment can induce psychological recovery and reduce stress/fatigue.
findings.quote: while showing a negative relationship with TSI.

findings.antecedent: Physical characteristics (Grey ratio, Loudness, LAeq, LA5-A95, Water ratio)
findings.mechanism: Decreased Grey ratio, Loudness, LAeq, LA5-A95, and increased Water ratio are associated with increased psychological restoration (e.g., being away from, valence, positive affect) and decreased arousal and negative affect. Explanatory power: 19%.
findings.quote: the physical characteristics and psychological restoration model, as in Fig. 6(a), can be used. The order of Grey ratio (-0.99) > Loudness (-0.89) > LAeq (-0.85) > LA5-A95 (0.59) > Water ratio (0.57) exhibits the order of importance

findings.antecedent: Audio-visual element identification (Traffic noise, Other noise, Human sound, Music, Birdsongs, Water sound, Wind sound, Vehicle, Building, People, Open space, Vegetation, Water space, Sky)
findings.mechanism: Decreased artificial audio-visual elements and increased natural audio-visual elements are associated with increased psychological restoration (e.g., being away from, valence, positive affect) and decreased arousal and negative affect. Explanatory power: 17%.
findings.quote: the audio-visual identification and psychological restoration factor showed a high correlation of 0.72

findings.antecedent: Audio-visual element identification (Traffic noise, Other noise, Human sound, Music, Birdsongs, Water sound, Wind sound, Vehicle, Building, People, Open space, Vegetation, Water space, Sky)
findings.mechanism: The relationship between audio-visual identification and physiological restoration was weak, with only 2% of variance explained, suggesting low practical significance.
findings.quote: physiological restoration effects were low (0.02% of variance explained)

findings.antecedent: Perceived affective quality (Detrimental soundscape, Discomfort landscape, Tranquil soundscape, Spatial/Natural landscape)
findings.mechanism: Decreased detrimental soundscape and discomforting landscape, and increased tranquil soundscape and spatial/natural landscape are associated with increased psychological restoration (e.g., fascination, being away to/from, valence, positive affect) and decreased arousal and negative affect. Explanatory power: 21%.
findings.quote: the perceived affective quality factor and psychological restoration factor was high (0.78)

findings.mechanism: Increased supportive soundscape is associated with increased compatibility, fascination, and positive affect. Explanatory power: 4%.
findings.quote: the supportive soundscape was identified as an important variable in perceived affective quality, as shown in Fig. 6 (e), and compatibility, fascination, and positive affect increased as the supportive soundscape increased.

findings.antecedent: Perceived affective quality (Detrimental soundscape, Tranquil soundscape, Discomfort landscape)
findings.mechanism: Detrimental and tranquil soundscapes, and discomforting landscapes are important variables in perceived affective quality, with mixed effects on psychological restoration. Explanatory power: 1%.
findings.quote: detrimental and tranquil soundscapes, and discomforting landscapes were identified as important variables in perceived affective quality

findings.antecedent: Perceived affective quality (Supportive soundscape, Tranquil soundscape, Attractive landscape, Spatial/Natural landscape, Detrimental soundscape, Discomfort landscape)
findings.mechanism: Increased supportive/tranquil soundscape and attractive/spatial-natural landscape, and decreased detrimental/discomforting landscape are associated with increased TP, SDNN, and decreased TSI, LF, HR, a/ß ratio. Explanatory power: 2%.
findings.quote: The explanatory power of perceived affective quality was low, with 2% of the variance of psychological restoration explained by the factor.

findings.antecedent: Overall environmental quality (Overall impression, Appropriateness, Sound satisfaction, Scenic beauty, Visual satisfaction)
findings.mechanism: Increased overall impression, appropriateness, sound satisfaction, scenic beauty, and visual satisfaction are associated with increased psychological restoration (e.g., being away to/from, valence, arousal, fascination, positive affect) and decreased negative affect. Explanatory power: 22%.
findings.quote: the overall environmental quality factor and psy- chological restoration factor showed a high correlation of 0.74

findings.consequent: Psychological restoration (Valence, Scope, Dominance, Fascination, Being away to, Compatibility, Arousal)
findings.mechanism: Improved status of infrastructure is associated with increased psychological restoration (e.g., valence, scope, dominance, fascination, being away to, compatibility, arousal). Explanatory power: 9%.
findings.quote: it was observed in the second pair that compatibility and dominance increased as the status of infrastructure was improved

findings.mechanism: Individual characteristics explained under 2% of the variance of psycho-physiological responses, showing low explanatory power.
findings.quote: individual character- istics explained under 2% of the variance of psycho-physiological re- sponses in most groups, thus showing low explanatory power.

stimuli.description: 360-degree audio-visual simulations of 9 urban (high-density commercial, low-density commercial, business), waterfront (river, wetland, ocean), and green (forest, valley, temple) environments. Visuals were 8k resolution, audio was 4-channel ambisonic.

limitations: Study conducted with participants aged 20-29 years, limiting generalizability to other age groups.
Findings may not reflect sociocultural differences as all participants were Korean and lived in a city.
Investigated short-term responses, necessitating long-term studies.
Used HMD headphone-based VR technology; more immersive AR/MR technologies might yield different results.
Only analyzed mean brain wave values; future research should explore a and b waves in different brain regions or functional connectivity.
Did not assess other physiological responses like blood, hormones, and brain images.
